article_title: M1 recruitment during interleaved practice is important for encoding, not just consolidation, of skill memory
citation: Taewon Kim, Hakjoo Kim, Benjamin A. Philip & David L. Wright. (2024). M1 recruitment during interleaved practice is important for encoding, not just consolidation, of skill memory. npj Science of Learning 9, 77. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-024-00290-2
title: M1 plays a broad role in motor skill memory, supporting encoding during interleaved practice as well as offline consolidation
description: The article proposes that primary motor cortex contributes to "multiple mechanisms inﬂuencing both online and ofﬂine behavioral outcomes" in motor skill learning. Traditionally, M1's role in interleaved practice was ascribed to offline consolidation; this study shows inhibiting M1 during interleaved practice instead impedes "the construction of a novel motor memory yet preserves effective consolidation". The account holds that M1 and dorsal premotor cortex are both important for developing motor sequence representations across training, even though M1 may not itself store the post-learning representations.
requirements: Interleaved practice with frequent switching between to-be-learned skills during training, so that M1 is engaged during encoding of sequence knowledge
constraints: The article notes tDCS montage might have inadvertently affected PMd or SMA, so the disruption could reflect inhibiting PMd or SMA–M1 connectivity rather than an independent effect at M1
The inhibitory effects of ctDCS on M1 might diminish over time as the motor system adapts by recruiting non-M1 sensorimotor areas such as PMd
target_learners: Adults learning novel motor sequences (right-handed undergraduate students in the study)
target_learning_goals: Retention and encoding of novel motor skill memory
examples: Fifty-four participants practiced three 6-item discrete sequence production tasks in RP-Sham, IP-Sham, or IP-ctDCS groups, with retention tests at 5 min, 6 h, and 24 h
